issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking enhanced land-acquisition compensation cannot establish a higher market value by relying on other lands without evidence that they are comparable in location, quality, and potential.
material_facts: The claimant appealed seeking compensation above the amount assessed by the High Court, relying on decisions concerning land in the same village and in neighboring villages.

The Reference Court found that the acquired land was agricultural, lacked electrical and municipal water connections, and was about six kilometres from the main road; some lands relied on as comparators were closer to the road and to developed areas.
The claimant produced no site plan or other evidence establishing that the acquired land was similarly situated to land in another village whose award he relied on.
The High Court had assessed compensation at the rate sought by the claimant, relying on an earlier judgment concerning land in the same village.
The Supreme Court found no cogent basis to interfere with the Reference Court’s findings or to award further enhancement.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not establish that the comparator lands were sufficiently similar to justify the higher valuation sought; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1) and 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed as at the notification date, from the perspective of the owner who parts with the land, taking account of its existing use, geographical situation, advantages, disadvantages, and potential that is not remote, while excluding advantages arising from the acquisition purpose. A claimant bears the burden of producing relevant evidence, and a court cannot grant compensation merely on the claimant’s request or on conjecture unsupported by the record. Comparator transactions or awards can guide valuation only where the lands are shown to be similar; location, distance, frontage, and other advantages may justify different values, and belting may be appropriate for large or non-contiguous acquisitions. The Court relied on Sections 9 and 23 and on Raja Vyricheria Narayana Gajapatraju Bahadur Garu v. Revenue Divisional Officer, Vizianagaram, AIR 1939 PC 98; Adusumilli Gopalkrishna v. Spl. Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition), AIR 1980 SC 1870; Thakur Kamta Prasad Singh v. State of Bihar, AIR 1976 SC 2219; Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Karigowda, AIR 2010 SC 2322; Charan Das v. H.P. Housing & Urban Development Authority, (2010) 13 SCC 398; Trishala Jain v. State of Uttaranchal, AIR 2011 SC 2458; Viluben Jhalejar Contractor v. State of Gujarat, AIR 2005 SC 2214; Executive Engineer, Karnataka Housing Board v. Land Acquisition Officer, AIR 2011 SC 781; Bilkis v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 12 SCC 646; Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, AIR 2012 SC 2709; Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. v. G. Mohan Reddy, (2010) 15 SCC 412; Ashrafi v. State of Haryana, AIR 2013 SC 3654; Sher Singh v. State of Haryana, AIR 1991 SC 2048; Executive Engineer (Electrical), Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner & Land Acquisition Officer, (2010) 15 SCC 60; Ramanlal Deochand Shah v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2013 SC 3452; Jawajee Nagnatham v. Revenue Divisional Officer, (1994) 4 SCC 595; and Land Acquisition Officer & Sub-Collector, Gadwal v. Sreelatha Bhoopal, (1997) 9 SCC 628.

rule.if: land_compensation_appeal and claimant_seeks_enhancement and claimant_lacks_comparator_similarity_proof and comparator_lands_have_location_advantages

predicates.land_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking review of compensation fixed for compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.claimant_seeks_enhancement: The claimant asked for compensation higher than the amount already assessed.
predicates.claimant_lacks_comparator_similarity_pro: The claimant did not provide evidence establishing that the acquired land was comparable to the lands relied on for a higher valuation.
predicates.comparator_lands_have_location_advantage: The record showed that the comparator lands had location advantages not shared by the acquired land.
predicates.enhancement_denied: The court denies the claimant’s request for a higher valuation.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks enhanced compensation in a land-compensation appeal but does not prove that the comparator lands are similar and those lands have location advantages, the court denies enhancement.
